claim: Protein phosphorylation is critical for cellular regulatory mechanisms.
source: Protein phosphorylation, critical for cellular regulatory mechanisms, is implicated in various diseases.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Protein phosphorylation is implicated in various diseases.
source: Protein phosphorylation, critical for cellular regulatory mechanisms, is implicated in various diseases.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Osteopontin phosphorylation level declined in hypo- and hyper-phosphatemia mouse models exhibiting skeletal deformities.
source: Here, osteopontin phosphorylation level declined in hypo- and hyper- phosphatemia mouse models exhibiting skeletal deformities.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study presented in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Phosphorylation increased cohesion between osteopontin polymers.
source: Phosphorylation increased cohesion between osteopontin polymers, and adhesion of osteopontin to hydroxyapatite, enhancing energy dissipation.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study presented in the abstract and supported by AFM-FS experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Phosphorylation increased adhesion of osteopontin to hydroxyapatite.
source: Phosphorylation increased cohesion between osteopontin polymers, and adhesion of osteopontin to hydroxyapatite, enhancing energy dissipation.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study presented in the abstract and supported by AFM-FS experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Phosphorylation of osteopontin enhances energy dissipation.
source: Phosphorylation increased cohesion between osteopontin polymers, and adhesion of osteopontin to hydroxyapatite, enhancing energy dissipation.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study presented in the abstract and supported by AFM-FS experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Fracture toughness increased with ex-vivo phosphorylation of wildtype mouse bones.
source: Fracture toughness, a measure of bone's mechanical competence, increased with ex-vivo phosphorylation of wildtype mouse bones and declined with ex-vivo dephosphorylation.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study presented in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Fracture toughness declined with ex-vivo dephosphorylation of wildtype mouse bones.
source: Fracture toughness, a measure of bone's mechanical competence, increased with ex-vivo phosphorylation of wildtype mouse bones and declined with ex-vivo dephosphorylation.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study presented in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: In osteopontin-deficient mice, global matrix phosphorylation level was not associated with toughness.
source: In osteopontin-deficient mice, global matrix phosphorylation level was not associated with toughness.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study presented in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8b.

claim: Phosphorylated osteopontin promotes fracture toughness in a dose-dependent manner through increased interfacial bond formation.
source: Our findings suggest that phosphorylated osteopontin promotes fracture toughness in a dose-dependent manner through increased interfacial bond formation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data shown in Figure 8a and AFM-FS studies.

claim: In the absence of osteopontin, phosphorylation increases electrostatic repulsion.
source: In the absence of osteopontin, phosphorylation increases electrostatic repulsion, and likely protein alignment and interfilament distance leading to decreased fracture resistance.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data shown in Figures 4 and 5 for Opn KO mice.

claim: In the absence of osteopontin, phosphorylation likely increases protein alignment and interfilament distance leading to decreased fracture resistance.
source: In the absence of osteopontin, phosphorylation increases electrostatic repulsion, and likely protein alignment and interfilament distance leading to decreased fracture resistance.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion drawn from the experimental data and comparison with neurofilament studies.

claim: Different levels of phosphorylation of matrix proteins play a critical role in coordinating calcification processes in normally mineralized bone tissues.
source: In particular, it has been postulated that different levels of phosphorylation of matrix proteins play a critical role in coordinating calcification processes in normally (Murshed et al., 2004; Clarke, 2008; Murshed and McKee, 2010; Nudelman et al., 2010; Addison et al., 2010; Deng et al., 2013) and pathologically (Boskey, 2013; Bertazzo et al., 2013) mineralized bone tissues either independently and/or in combination with collagen.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Different levels of phosphorylation of matrix proteins play a critical role in coordinating calcification processes in pathologically mineralized bone tissues.
source: In particular, it has been postulated that different levels of phosphorylation of matrix proteins play a critical role in coordinating calcification processes in normally (Murshed et al., 2004; Clarke, 2008; Murshed and McKee, 2010; Nudelman et al., 2010; Addison et al., 2010; Deng et al., 2013) and pathologically (Boskey, 2013; Bertazzo et al., 2013) mineralized bone tissues either independently and/or in combination with collagen.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Phosphoproteins accumulate at the interfaces found across bone's hierarchical levels.
source: These phosphoproteins also accumulate at the interfaces found across bone's hierarchical levels (McKee and Nanci, 1996; Thurner et al., 2009; Thurner, 2009), but it remains unclear as to how their phosphorylation levels influence the mechanical properties of bone.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Global phosphorylation level varied between cortical and trabecular bone.
source: Global phosphorylation level varied between cortical and trabecular bone (Sroga and Vashishth, 2016), declined with age, and was associated with an increase in age-related skeletal fragility (Sroga and Vashishth, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research by the authors.

claim: Global phosphorylation level declined with age.
source: Global phosphorylation level varied between cortical and trabecular bone (Sroga and Vashishth, 2016), declined with age, and was associated with an increase in age-related skeletal fragility (Sroga and Vashishth, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research by the authors.

claim: Global phosphorylation level was associated with an increase in age-related skeletal fragility.
source: Global phosphorylation level varied between cortical and trabecular bone (Sroga and Vashishth, 2016), declined with age, and was associated with an increase in age-related skeletal fragility (Sroga and Vashishth, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research by the authors.

claim: Hyp mice display low-serum phosphate and accumulation of osteopontin.
source: Hyp mice – the murine analog of X-linked hypophosphatemia (XLH) – display low-serum phosphate and accumulation of osteopontin (OPN) (Barros et al., 2013), a well-known noncollagenous protein serving as a powerful inhibitor of mineralization, and a key determinant of bone's resistance to fracture.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Osteopontin is a powerful inhibitor of mineralization.
source: Hyp mice – the murine analog of X-linked hypophosphatemia (XLH) – display low-serum phosphate and accumulation of osteopontin (OPN) (Barros et al., 2013), a well-known noncollagenous protein serving as a powerful inhibitor of mineralization, and a key determinant of bone's resistance to fracture.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Osteopontin is a key determinant of bone's resistance to fracture.
source: Hyp mice – the murine analog of X-linked hypophosphatemia (XLH) – display low-serum phosphate and accumulation of osteopontin (OPN) (Barros et al., 2013), a well-known noncollagenous protein serving as a powerful inhibitor of mineralization, and a key determinant of bone's resistance to fracture.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Fgf23-/- mice are hyperphosphatemic and show accumulation of OPN.
source: In contrast to Hyp mice, fibroblast growth factor 23-deficient mice (Fgf23-/- mice) are hyperphosphatemic, but like the Hyp mice also show accumulation of OPN (Yuan et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Both Hyp and Fgf23-/- mice exhibit a soft-bone (osteomalacia) phenotype.
source: Both of these phosphate-handling disease models exhibit a soft-bone (osteomalacia) phenotype and display decreased cortical area, thickness, and strength (Liu et al., 2016; Murali et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Both Hyp and Fgf23-/- mice display decreased cortical area, thickness, and strength.
source: Both of these phosphate-handling disease models exhibit a soft-bone (osteomalacia) phenotype and display decreased cortical area, thickness, and strength (Liu et al., 2016; Murali et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The hypophosphatasia mouse model (Alpl−/− mice) displays mineralization deficiencies characterized by rickets/osteomalacia.
source: The hypophosphatasia mouse model (Alpl−/− mice) displays mineralization deficiencies characterized by rickets/osteomalacia as well as elevated levels of inorganic pyrophosphate (PPi).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the mouse model.

claim: The hypophosphatasia mouse model (Alpl−/− mice) displays elevated levels of inorganic pyrophosphate (PPi).
source: The hypophosphatasia mouse model (Alpl−/− mice) displays mineralization deficiencies characterized by rickets/osteomalacia as well as elevated levels of inorganic pyrophosphate (PPi).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the mouse model.

claim: Alpl−/− mice show increased levels of phosphorylated OPN compared to wild type (WT) mice.
source: The Alpl−/− mice also show increased levels of phosphorylated OPN compared to wild type (WT) mice (Narisawa et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Opn KO mice show elevated levels of PPi despite having more mineralized osteoid than wildtype (WT) controls.
source: Interestingly, Opn KO mice also show elevated levels of PPi despite having more mineralized osteoid than wildtype (WT) controls (Harmey et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: The degree of OPN phosphorylation has significant effects on its structure and physiological function.
source: The degree of OPN phosphorylation has significant effects on its structure and physiological function (Kazanecki et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Osteoclast adhesion is increased with phosphorylation of OPN.
source: For example, osteoclast adhesion is increased with phosphorylation (Katayama et al., 1998) and correlates with the extent of bone resorption (Razzouk et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Osteoclast adhesion correlates with the extent of bone resorption.
source: For example, osteoclast adhesion is increased with phosphorylation (Katayama et al., 1998) and correlates with the extent of bone resorption (Razzouk et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Hydroxyapatite (HA) crystal formation and growth are inhibited by OPN in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Hydroxyapatite (HA) crystal formation and growth are inhibited by OPN in a dose-dependent manner (Hunter et al., 1994), and dephosphorylation of OPN abolishes the inhibitory effect of OPN on HA formation by at least 40-fold (Razzouk et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Dephosphorylation of OPN abolishes the inhibitory effect of OPN on HA formation by at least 40-fold.
source: Hydroxyapatite (HA) crystal formation and growth are inhibited by OPN in a dose-dependent manner (Hunter et al., 1994), and dephosphorylation of OPN abolishes the inhibitory effect of OPN on HA formation by at least 40-fold (Razzouk et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: OPN has been shown to play a mechanical role in bone, influencing its resistance to fracture.
source: In addition to bone resorption and mineralization, OPN has been shown to play a mechanical role in bone, influencing its resistance to fracture (Duvall et al., 2007; Thurner et al., 2010; Poundarik et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The negatively charged phosphate groups of serine and threonine residues on OPN bind to multivalent positive ions on hydroxyapatite.
source: The negatively charged phosphate groups of serine and threonine residues on OPN bind to multivalent positive ions on hydroxyapatite, and this interaction is part of a bonding/cohesion process that limits separation of mineralized collagen fibrils during mechanical loading (Zappone et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: The interaction between OPN phosphate groups and hydroxyapatite is part of a bonding/cohesion process that limits separation of mineralized collagen fibrils during mechanical loading.
source: The negatively charged phosphate groups of serine and threonine residues on OPN bind to multivalent positive ions on hydroxyapatite, and this interaction is part of a bonding/cohesion process that limits separation of mineralized collagen fibrils during mechanical loading (Zappone et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Large, covalently crosslinked networks are formed between neighboring OPN molecules and between OPN and other bone matrix proteins by transglutaminase.
source: Also important in this bone-toughening process are large, covalently crosslinked (by transglutaminase) networks formed between neighboring OPN molecules and between OPN and other bone matrix proteins (Kaartinen et al., 1999; Kaartinen et al., 1997; Kaartinen et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Networks of crosslinked OPN polymers are abundantly present in bone.
source: Networks of crosslinked OPN polymers are abundantly present in bone, and may reside in the interfibrillar collagenous matrix, at cell-matrix interfaces, and in interfacial cement lines (Kaartinen et al., 2002; Goldsmith et al., 2002) where they may be critical for maintaining the overall strength of bone tissue (Kaartinen et al., 1999; Hoac et al., 2017; Cavelier et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Networks of crosslinked OPN polymers may reside in the interfibrillar collagenous matrix, at cell-matrix interfaces, and in interfacial cement lines.
source: Networks of crosslinked OPN polymers are abundantly present in bone, and may reside in the interfibrillar collagenous matrix, at cell-matrix interfaces, and in interfacial cement lines (Kaartinen et al., 2002; Goldsmith et al., 2002) where they may be critical for maintaining the overall strength of bone tissue (Kaartinen et al., 1999; Hoac et al., 2017; Cavelier et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Networks of crosslinked OPN polymers may be critical for maintaining the overall strength of bone tissue.
source: Networks of crosslinked OPN polymers are abundantly present in bone, and may reside in the interfibrillar collagenous matrix, at cell-matrix interfaces, and in interfacial cement lines (Kaartinen et al., 2002; Goldsmith et al., 2002) where they may be critical for maintaining the overall strength of bone tissue (Kaartinen et al., 1999; Hoac et al., 2017; Cavelier et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Phosphorylation of OPN is highly variable across different tissues.
source: Analysis of different tissues revealed that phosphorylation of OPN is highly variable, and typically only some of the potential phosphorylation sites are occupied in vivo (Neame and Butler, 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Typically only some of the potential phosphorylation sites on OPN are occupied in vivo.
source: Analysis of different tissues revealed that phosphorylation of OPN is highly variable, and typically only some of the potential phosphorylation sites are occupied in vivo (Neame and Butler, 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Mineral-bound OPN increased in the bone matrix of both Hyp and Fgf23-/- mice compared to WT controls.
source: In the bone matrix of both Hyp and Fgf23-/- mice, we found that mineral-bound OPN increased (Figure 1a) but global phosphorylation decreased (Figure 1b) as compared to WT controls.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: Global phosphorylation decreased in the bone matrix of both Hyp and Fgf23-/- mice compared to WT controls.
source: In the bone matrix of both Hyp and Fgf23-/- mice, we found that mineral-bound OPN increased (Figure 1a) but global phosphorylation decreased (Figure 1b) as compared to WT controls.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: Despite the accumulation of OPN in Hyp and Fgf23-/- mice, the proportion of phosphorylated OPN was reduced compared to the bone of WT mice.
source: In addition, the post-immunoprecipation results show that despite the accumulation of OPN in Hyp and Fgf23-/- mice (Figure 1c), the proportion of phosphorylated OPN was reduced compared to the bone of WT mice (Figure 1d).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study supported by post-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figures 1c and 1d.

claim: The global phosphorylation level in bone matrix increased in both WT and Opn KO genotypes with ex-vivo casein kinase-II (CKII) phosphorylation.
source: The global phosphorylation level in bone matrix increased in both genotypes with ex-vivo casein kinase-II (CKII) phosphorylation (WT-phosphorylated vs. WT-nonphosphorylated control, p=0.008; Opn KO-phosphorylated vs. Opn KO-nonphosphorylated control, p=0.007) (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2a with statistical significance.

claim: A significant reduction in phosphoproteins was observed with ex-vivo dephosphorylation by alkaline phosphatase in both WT and Opn KO mice.
source: We observed a significant reduction in phosphoproteins with ex-vivo dephosphorylation by alkaline phosphatase (WT-dephosphorylated vs. WT-nondephosphorylated control, p=0.033; Opn KO-dephosphorylated vs. Opn KO-nondephosphorylated control, p=0.006) (Figure 3a).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3a with statistical significance.

claim: A significant difference in dephosphorylation was observed between delta-WT and delta-Opn KO.
source: Although the change in ex-vivo phosphorylation between WT and Opn KO (delta-WT vs. delta-Opn KO, Figure 2b) was not statistically significant, we observed a significant difference in dephosphorylation between delta-WT and delta-Opn KO (Figure 3b), indicating that OPN-deficient bone can be modified to a greater extent than WT bone, likely attributable to increased permeability of enzymes into bones lacking OPN.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3b.

claim: OPN-deficient bone can be modified to a greater extent than WT bone, likely attributable to increased permeability of enzymes into bones lacking OPN.
source: Although the change in ex-vivo phosphorylation between WT and Opn KO (delta-WT vs. delta-Opn KO, Figure 2b) was not statistically significant, we observed a significant difference in dephosphorylation between delta-WT and delta-Opn KO (Figure 3b), indicating that OPN-deficient bone can be modified to a greater extent than WT bone, likely attributable to increased permeability of enzymes into bones lacking OPN.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data showing greater dephosphorylation in Opn KO bones.

claim: Higher fracture toughness was observed with phosphorylation of WT bones.
source: We observed higher fracture toughness with phosphorylation of WT bones (WT-phosphorylated vs. WT-nonphosphorylated control, p=0.009).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4 with statistical significance.

claim: Toughness declined in Opn KO mice following ex-vivo phosphorylation.
source: In contrast, toughness declined in Opn KO mice following ex-vivo phosphorylation (Opn KO-phosphorylated vs. Opn KO-nonphosphorylated control, p=0.025) indicating that phosphorylation of other bone matrix proteins in the absence of OPN did not improve the fracture resistance of bone (Figure 4).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4 with statistical significance.

claim: Phosphorylation of other bone matrix proteins in the absence of OPN did not improve the fracture resistance of bone.
source: In contrast, toughness declined in Opn KO mice following ex-vivo phosphorylation (Opn KO-phosphorylated vs. Opn KO-nonphosphorylated control, p=0.025) indicating that phosphorylation of other bone matrix proteins in the absence of OPN did not improve the fracture resistance of bone (Figure 4).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing decreased toughness in phosphorylated Opn KO bones.

claim: Ex-vivo dephosphorylation caused a decrease in fracture toughness for the WT group.
source: Ex-vivo dephosphorylation caused a decrease in fracture toughness for the WT group (WT-dephosphorylated vs. WT-nondephosphorylated control, p=0.012) (Figure 5)
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5 with statistical significance.

claim: An increase in fracture toughness was observed for Opn KO mice following ex-vivo dephosphorylation.
source: while an increase in fracture toughness was observed for Opn KO mice (Opn KO-dephosphorylated vs. Opn KO-nondephosphorylated control, p=0.037).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5 with statistical significance.

claim: At pH 8.5, both OPN and hydroxyapatite (HA) surfaces are negatively charged.
source: At pH 8.5, both OPN and hydroxyapatite (HA) surfaces are negatively charged.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the charge properties of these materials at this pH.

claim: Under high Ca2+ concentration at pH 8.5, the detachment energy increased more significantly as compared to H2O and Na+ environments.
source: Under high Ca2+ concentration, the detachment energy increased more significantly as compared to H2O and Na+ environments.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the AFM-FS study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: At pH 6.0, the protein and HA bear opposite charges.
source: At pH 6.0 however, the protein and HA bear opposite charges.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the charge properties of these materials at this pH.

claim: The slightly acidic pH leads to a moderate dissolution of HA over time.
source: The slightly acidic pH lead to a moderate dissolution of HA over time, and therefore, it is expected that Ca2+ ions are present in solution from the beginning of the experiment.
evidence: This is an inference based on known chemical properties of HA at acidic pH.

claim: Further addition of Ca2+ ions at pH 6.0 decreased energy dissipation attributable to the reduction of sacrificial bond formation and increased repulsion between OPN and HA.
source: Further addition of Ca2+ ions decreased energy dissipation attributable to the reduction of sacrificial bond formation (Gao et al., 2003) (increase of effectively positively charged sites in OPN) as well as increased repulsion between OPN and HA.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the AFM-FS study supported by experimental data and citation to prior research on sacrificial bonds.

claim: Dephosphorylated OPN in Ca2+ solution at pH 7.4 showed a decline in energy dissipation as compared to native OPN.
source: These results were also confirmed by the decline in energy dissipation that was observed for dephosphorylated OPN in Ca2+ solution at pH 7.4 as compared to native OPN, as well as dephosphorylated OPN in Na+ solution at pH 7.4, all on mica substrates.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the AFM-FS study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The balance between Ca2+ ions in solution and the availability of negatively charged groups are both important for energy dissipation within the OPN network as well as at the OPN-HA interface.
source: Thus, the balance between Ca2+ ions in solution and the availability of negatively charged groups are both important for energy dissipation within the OPN network as well as at the OPN-HA interface.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the AFM-FS experimental data.

claim: Cation-mediated crosslinks are formed between two binding regions on one OPN polymer, multiple OPN polymers, and OPN and charged surface ions on HA.
source: First, cation-mediated crosslinks are formed between two binding regions on one OPN polymer, multiple OPN polymers, and OPN and charged surface ions on HA (e.g., Ca2+, Na+) (Figure 6—figure supplement 3; Fantner et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a mechanistic explanation supported by citation to prior research and illustrated in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: Salt-bridges are weak, but reformable sacrificial bonds that prevent portions of OPN polymers from rupturing and debonding of OPN from HA during repetitive mechanical loading.
source: These salt-bridges are weak, but reformable sacrificial bonds that prevent portions of OPN polymers from rupturing (cohesion of the OPN meshwork) and debonding of OPN from HA during repetitive mechanical loading (Zappone et al., 2008; Fantner et al., 2007; Lai et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a mechanistic explanation supported by citations to prior research.

claim: In the presence of Ca2+ ions and when both phosphorylated milk OPN and HA are negatively charged, detachment energy increased significantly.
source: In the presence of Ca2+ ions and when both phosphorylated milk OPN and HA are negatively charged, detachment energy increased significantly.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the AFM-FS study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The increase in detachment energy was also observed between OPN and mica substrate.
source: The increase in detachment energy was also observed between OPN and mica substrate (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the AFM-FS study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Ca2+-mediated crosslinks were formed between OPN polymers, which increased cohesion of the OPN meshwork, indicated by higher detachment energy.
source: Ca2+-mediated crosslinks were also formed between OPN polymers, which increased cohesion of the OPN meshwork, indicated by higher detachment energy (Figure 6—figure supplement 2), which is generally associated with loading of multiple molecules in parallel (Fantner et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the AFM-FS study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2 and citation to prior research.

claim: Dephosphorylation of milk OPN or reversing the charge on HA both resulted in decreased energy dissipation.
source: Dephosphosphorylation of milk OPN or reversing the charge on HA both resulted in decreased energy dissipation (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the AFM-FS study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Phosphorylation of WT bone specimens ex-vivo caused an approximate 18% increase in fracture toughness.
source: Similarly, phosphorylation of WT bone specimens ex-vivo under our experimental conditions caused an approximate 18% increase in fracture toughness (Figure 4a)
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Dephosphorylation of WT bone specimens decreased toughness by 25%.
source: whereas, dephosphorylation decreased toughness by 25% (Figure 5a).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5a.

claim: Phosphorylation is enabling various matrix/mineral interactions, and hence, dissipating energy.
source: These results suggest that phosphorylation is enabling various matrix/mineral interactions, and hence, dissipating energy.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on fracture toughness and AFM-FS studies.

claim: Phosphorylation can alter protein network conformation, the mechanical behavior of the organic matrix, and consequently the macroscopic fracture toughness of bone.
source: Second, phosphorylation can alter protein network conformation, the mechanical behavior of the organic matrix, and consequently the macroscopic fracture toughness of bone (Thurner et al., 2009; Fantner et al., 2007; Fisher et al., 2001).
evidence: This is a mechanistic explanation supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) and their phosphorylation status can alter neurofilament protein alignment and distance between filaments, resulting in changed energy dissipation of the network.
source: A recent experimental study (Malka-Gibor et al., 2017) demonstrated that intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) and their phosphorylation status can alter neurofilament protein alignment and distance between filaments, resulting in changed energy dissipation of the network (Figure 7).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research and illustrated in Figure 7.

claim: Both collagen and neurofilaments are bundled network systems that interact with IDPs.
source: Both collagen and neurofilaments are bundled network systems that interact with IDPs (Laser-Azogui et al., 2015; Orgel et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Non-collagenous proteins in bone matrix such as small integrin-binding ligand, N-linked glycoproteins (SIBLINGs) are IDPs.
source: For example, non-collagenous proteins in bone matrix such as small integrin-binding ligand, N-linked glycoproteins (SIBLINGs) are IDPs, interact with collagen, and gain more folded features when post-translationally modified (phosphorylation, glycation, acetylation, sulfation, cleavage) (Boskey and Villarreal-Ramirez, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: SIBLINGs interact with collagen and gain more folded features when post-translationally modified.
source: For example, non-collagenous proteins in bone matrix such as small integrin-binding ligand, N-linked glycoproteins (SIBLINGs) are IDPs, interact with collagen, and gain more folded features when post-translationally modified (phosphorylation, glycation, acetylation, sulfation, cleavage) (Boskey and Villarreal-Ramirez, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: In the presence of excess Ca2+ ions strong cohesion and excessive crosslinking of the OPN meshwork reduces the stretching ability of the meshwork, leading to shorter pulls, increased repulsion of all positive sites, which likely increased distance in the meshwork, and diminished detachment energy.
source: Our AFM-FS studies showed that in the presence of excess Ca2+ ions strong cohesion and excessive crosslinking of the OPN meshwork reduces the stretching ability of the meshwork, leading to shorter pulls, increased repulsion of all positive sites, which likely increased distance in the meshwork, and diminished detachment energy.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the AFM-FS experimental data.

claim: The increase in global phosphorylation of other bone matrix proteins in the absence of OPN may potentially result in increased protein alignment and larger interfilament distance between mineralized collagen fibrils, to a detrimental degree that decreases matrix interaction, energy dissipation, and consequently fracture resistance in osteopontin-deficient mice.
source: We postulate that the increase in global phosphorylation of other bone matrix proteins in the absence of OPN ( e.g. other SIBLING matrix proteins) may also potentially result in increased protein alignment and larger interfilament distance between mineralized collagen fibrils, to a detrimental degree that decreases matrix interaction, energy dissipation, and consequently fracture resistance in osteopontin-deficient mice (Figure 4).
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion drawn from the experimental data and comparison with neurofilament studies.

claim: A non-linear dose response relationship exists between the level of global matrix phosphorylation and bone fracture toughness in WT mice.
source: We observed a non-linear dose response relationship between the level of global matrix phosphorylation and bone fracture toughness in WT mice (Figure 8a).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8a.

claim: Phosphorylation explained ~36% of the variance in fracture toughness in WT mice.
source: Phosphorylation explained ~36% of the variance in fracture toughness and this relationship was not observed in the absence of OPN (Figure 8b).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 8.

claim: The relationship between phosphorylation and fracture toughness was not observed in the absence of OPN.
source: Phosphorylation explained ~36% of the variance in fracture toughness and this relationship was not observed in the absence of OPN (Figure 8b).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8b.

claim: Adhesion is not only dependent on the charge of OPN and HA under a certain environment but also the availability of free Ca2+ ions.
source: The AFM-FS studies show that adhesion is not only dependent on the charge of OPN and HA under a certain environment but also the availability of free Ca2+ ions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the AFM-FS experimental data.

claim: Crosslinking of OPN by transglutaminase-2 enzyme (TG2) increases interfacial adhesion and toughness.
source: It has been previously shown that crosslinking of OPN by transglutaminase-2 enzyme (TG2) increases interfacial adhesion and toughness (Cavelier et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: OC inhibits TG2 crosslinking activity most likely by competing for the binding site on OPN.
source: However, OC inhibits TG2 crosslinking activity most likely by competing for the binding site on OPN (Kaartinen et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Ex-vivo phosphorylation of Opn KO mice bone decreased fracture toughness.
source: Although ex-vivo phosphorylation of Opn KO mice bone decreased fracture toughness (Figure 4a), and dephosphorylation increased toughness compared to the respective untreated Opn KO mice bone (Figure 5a), unlike WT, we did not observe an association between the level of global matrix phosphorylation and fracture toughness in these mice (Figure 8b).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Dephosphorylation of Opn KO mice bone increased toughness compared to the respective untreated Opn KO mice bone.
source: Although ex-vivo phosphorylation of Opn KO mice bone decreased fracture toughness (Figure 4a), and dephosphorylation increased toughness compared to the respective untreated Opn KO mice bone (Figure 5a), unlike WT, we did not observe an association between the level of global matrix phosphorylation and fracture toughness in these mice (Figure 8b).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5a.

claim: Excessive crosslinking can be detrimental to protein networks by increasing repulsion, interfilament distance, and stretching ability.
source: As noted above, excessive crosslinking can be detrimental to protein networks by increasing repulsion, interfilament distance, and stretching ability.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and comparison with neurofilament studies.

claim: Although global matrix level of phosphorylation affects fracture toughness, the contribution of phosphorylated OPN may be critical in the determination of bone toughness.
source: This data suggests that although global matrix level of phosphorylation affects fracture toughness, the contribution of phosphorylated OPN may be critical in the determination of bone toughness.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data comparing WT and Opn KO mice.

claim: The gross skeletal phenotype of Opn KO mice is normal compared to WT mice.
source: The gross skeletal phenotype of Opn KO mice is normal compared to WT mice (Rittling et al., 1998; Yoshitake et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Increased mineralization was found in some areas of cortical bone in Opn KO mice.
source: However, increased mineralization was found in some areas of cortical bone (Boskey et al., 2002), and the bones are mechanically weaker.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: The bones of Opn KO mice are mechanically weaker.
source: However, increased mineralization was found in some areas of cortical bone (Boskey et al., 2002), and the bones are mechanically weaker.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about Opn KO mice.

claim: The collagen structure in Opn KO mice was shown to be highly disorganized which further causes disorganization of mineral.
source: The collagen structure in Opn KO mice was also shown to be highly disorganized which further causes disorganization of mineral (Depalle et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: OPN in bone resides at its surfaces (including lining the lacuno-canalicular system) in the thin structure known as the lamina limitans, and throughout bulk bone.
source: OPN in bone resides at its surfaces (including lining the lacuno-canalicular system) in the thin structure known as the lamina limitans (McKee and Nanci, 1996), and throughout bulk bone.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Bovine milk OPN contains approximately 28 phosphorylation sites and all but a few residues in this motif are phosphorylated.
source: Bovine milk OPN contains approximately 28 phosphorylation sites and all but a few residues in this motif are phosphorylated.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about bovine milk OPN.

claim: The maximum-load method for measuring fracture toughness demonstrates the least variability compared to other methods.
source: Despite the fact that the maximum-load method for measuring fracture toughness demonstrates the least variability compared to other methods (Ritchie et al., 2008), there is inherent variability in fracture toughness tests.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Opn KO mice have lower fracture toughness compared to WT mice.
source: For example, we have shown with a larger sample size that Opn KO mice have lower fracture toughness compared to WT mice (Thurner et al., 2010; Poundarik et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research by the authors.

claim: Osteopontin and its phosphorylation level promotes fracture toughness of bone.
source: In conclusion, this study shows for the first time that osteopontin and its phosphorylation level promotes fracture toughness of bone.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study supported by all experimental data.

claim: The heterogeneity in osteopontin phosphorylation alters interfacial adhesion and cohesion of the OPN meshwork leading to increased or decreased energy dissipation.
source: The heterogeneity in osteopontin phosphorylation, alters interfacial adhesion and cohesion of the OPN meshwork leading to increased or decreased energy dissipation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: In the absence of osteopontin, phosphorylation and de-phosphorylation of other bone matrix proteins impact bone toughness in a binary stepwise manner.
source: In the absence of osteopontin, phosphorylation and de-phosphorylation of other bone matrix proteins impact bone toughness in a binary stepwise manner.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on Opn KO mice.

claim: Fracture toughness is a measure of bone's mechanical competence.
source: Fracture toughness, a measure of bone's mechanical competence, increased with ex-vivo phosphorylation of wildtype mouse bones and declined with ex-vivo dephosphorylation.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the field.

claim: At the nanoscale, major contributions to the intrinsic toughness of bone originate from the OPN-crosslinked protein networks and the formation of dilatational bands involving osteocalcin (OC)-osteopontin complexes.
source: In the context of the present work, at the nanoscale, major contributions to the intrinsic toughness of bone originate from the OPN-crosslinked protein networks (Cavelier et al., 2018; Fantner et al., 2007) and the formation of dilatational bands involving osteocalcin (OC)-osteopontin complexes (Poundarik et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The OC-OPN complex has been shown to provide high shear toughness and ductility to the interfibrillar interface.
source: The OC-OPN complex has been recently shown to provide high shear toughness and ductility to the interfibrillar interface (Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Both the OPN-crosslinked protein networks and the OC-OPN complex presumably work together to control deformation and separation of mineralized collagen fibrils.
source: Both the OPN-crosslinked protein networks and the OC-OPN complex presumably work together to control deformation and separation of mineralized collagen fibrils (Gao et al., 2003; Zimmermann et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a conclusion supported by citations to prior research.

claim: In bovine milk, OPN is subjected to proteolytic processing by proteinases such as thrombin, plasmin, cathepsin D or matrix metalloproteinases.
source: In bovine milk, OPN is subjected to proteolytic processing by proteinases such as thrombin (Grassinger et al., 2009), plasmin, cathepsin D or matrix metalloproteinases (Christensen et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The principal components of isolated OPN from bovine milk are N-terminal OPN fragments ending between residues 145 and 153 of the mature protein as well as the mature full-length protein.
source: The principal components are N-terminal OPN fragments ending between residues 145 and 153 of the mature protein as well as the mature full-length protein (Christensen and Sørensen, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior research.
